whatItFakes: P10 drive, perception, response and event-severity coefficients are prototype starting values without measured bounds.
why: A starting value is required for drives to form and fade; no instrument-matched source fixes these coefficients yet.
replacement: Coefficients checked against P9 life replays and real bereaved/harmed-cohort spreads of civic action.

whatItFakes: Drive formation as one scored choice among response rows (carry on, take up a cause, hold a grudge, guard family, prove oneself, answer a calling), using the shared chooser and trait-act table; the response set and goal pressures are prototype assumptions.
why: Event-born drives were zero in P8 (acceptance d); the decision path is real but its response set and weights are uncalibrated.
replacement: Researched Oct 24, 2026: the band the response pressures calibrate against is data/research/people/trauma-trajectories-2018.json (Galatzer-Levy, Huang and Bonanno, Clinical Psychology Review 2018: 65.7% resilient after a potential trauma, 95% interval 61.6 to 69.8), reported against the town's bereavement carry-on share by scripts/research/people-year.ts; the builder item people-drives-responses-against-research-bands sets the pressures. Response rows and pressures calibrated against documented responses to bereavement, job loss and injustice (P9 lives, panel studies). Calibrated Oct 24, 2026 (traits lead): the bereavement rules carry their own drive-fit multiple (responseBereavementFitScale 2.1) and the grudge fit is 1.7, so about two in three of the bereaved who can form a drive of their own carry on and 1.7 to 14.9% of the laid off hold a grudge (data/research/people/termination-claims-1998.json); the cause, guard and calling fits for every other event, the trait-lean gain and the illness, crime and injustice responses are still prototype values with no band.

whatItFakes: Trait-weighted perception channels (loss, others' distress, injustice, threat, persuasion) choosing which traits raise or lower an event's weight; channel membership is authored.
why: The owner approved bounded perception; no source maps these traits to event salience yet.
replacement: Researched Oct 24, 2026: no appraisal study with a trait-to-salience effect that converts to a channel weight was found (Europe PMC searches for a pooled neuroticism and perceived-stress or stress-reactivity estimate returned single studies only), so channel rows stay authored; the builder item people-drives-responses-against-research-bands starts with that search. Channel rows and weights validated against appraisal research and P9 replays. Oct 24, 2026 (traits lead): the injustice channel's directions (forgiving lowers, vindictive and defensive raise) agree in sign with the forgiveness meta-analysis (data/research/people/fehr-forgiveness-correlates-2010.json: trait forgiveness r = .30, agreeableness .22, neuroticism -.24, trait anger -.18 with forgiving an offender); the loss, others'-distress, threat and persuasion channels still have no study.

whatItFakes: Drive acts (tell someone, join, donate, volunteer, confront, seek standing) with prototype durations and consequences; outcomes beyond money, membership and relationships are not modeled.
why: Drives must move people, money and relationships inside the core; full group and civic procedures do not exist yet.
replacement: Researched Oct 24, 2026: the volunteer act's hours are SOURCED from the American Time Use Survey 2025, Table 1 (BLS): volunteerHours 2.18 hours per participant-day, data/research/people/atus-2025-volunteering.json, read by the volunteer-for-cause act in src/core2/data/drives.json; civic acts already read civicHours from the same row. ATUS has no category for telling someone about a cause, making a donation or a confrontation, so driveShareHours, donateHours and driveConfrontHours stay prototype. The group and civic procedures are people-stopgap-drives-missing-mechanic and people-stopgap-drives-cause-group-spending. Group, charity and civic engines whose procedures decide outcomes, with durations from ATUS.

whatItFakes: A resident founds a cause group instantly with no charter, registration, dues or officers.
why: Organizing needs a place for others to join; the nonprofit and association engine is not built.
replacement: An association engine with formation steps, registration law per place and membership rules.
resolution: Founding stays one act on a recorded drive (the found-cause-group act in src/core2/data/drives.json): the standing rule 'This is a game, not a spreadsheet' in AGENTS.md admits no charter, registration or dues step the golden path does not need and The Political Process does not have. The group's depth is where it reacts: the members who join and what the interest-groups engine does with it.

whatItFakes: Testifying at a hearing is a registered act row that is never offered.
why: Core2 has no hearings or legislature.
replacement: The legislature/committee module's hearing calendar offering testimony slots.
resolution: the act row is deleted. Testimony is a resident's remark at a hearing or meeting (the meetings module's remarks and hearings), chosen from the resident's own views, so a second drive act would be a parallel route.

whatItFakes: Running for office is a registered act row that is never offered.
why: Core2 has no elections or filing.
replacement: The elections module's filing and campaign acts.
resolution: the act row is deleted. Who runs is decided by the elections and candidacy modules (candidacy.ts, candidate-pool.ts, world-races), so a drive act would be a parallel route.

whatItFakes: Lobbying a legislator is a registered act row that is never offered.
why: Core2 has no legislature or member contact system.
replacement: The legislature module's member-contact and bill-sponsor acts.
resolution: the act row is deleted. Lobbying is the interest-groups module's contact with a legislator, so a drive act would be a parallel route.

whatItFakes: Only the opening chronic conditions, the serious-illness onset and the death of the Ruling 29/38/39 mortality rule run in core2; conditions beginning during life, coverage, poverty onset causes, injuries and births are absent.
why: P10 needs a real recorded death from illness; no core2 health engine exists.
replacement: A full core2 health engine ported per the P11 plan.

whatItFakes: Event impulses scale Holmes-Rahe life change units into core2 stress and mood impulses with tunable conversions.
why: Events need a sized emotional impact; the life-change ranking is sourced but its conversion to the affect scale is not.
replacement: A calibrated appraisal model checked against bereavement and illness affect trajectories.

whatItFakes: One base-rate scale (0.097, refit Oct 27, 2026 over twenty-four generated towns: 450 deaths against 446.0 expected) for every place; the chronic-condition weights were calibrated for the old shared threshold and are not refit, and single towns range from 0.3 to 1.9 of the table's count.
why: The owner replaced the shared threshold with personal resilience lines; totals must stay on the life table and a full recalibration of the condition pack has not been done.
replacement: A cohort calibration of base scale and condition weights together, checked across many places and ages against the life table.

whatItFakes: A founded cause group carries a structured key in its name field instead of a name.
why: Names must come from the English engine; no naming bank for groups exists in core2.
replacement: An English-engine naming bank for associations reading topic and place.
